Header:
Date: 2026-08-11
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya T., Eli C., Sofia M., Rahul G., Aisha V., and ~150 others across org
---
Summary:
Maya: quick welcome, state of company, big theme: focus on serving and unit economics, be transparent about hiring and priorities.
Sofia: product roadmap highlight: Dedicated GA expansion, Private VPC improvements, Optimize cost tooling.
Eli: infra notes, kernel/compilation work, recent incident, perf numbers.
Security: SOC2 progress and customer controls.
Q&A: mix of tactical and strategic, some cross-talk on pricing and dedicated pricing tiers.
---
Topics: Q2 results; Dedicated; Private; Security; Hiring; Customer benchmarks; Q&A
---
Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Speaker 1 (Maya): hey everyone, um hi, welcome to the August all hands. sorry running a couple minutes late there was, uh a calendar overlap. we have a packed agenda, i'm just gonna start with high level.
[00:18] Speaker 2 (Maya): Q2 ended on a mixed note, revenue up 23% quarter over quarter but net burn is still higher than we'd like, so the main theme is focus on unit economics and serving predictability, we want to make sure every team can point to the levers that improve latency and cost.
[00:38] Speaker 3 (Eli): quick infra note — we've been moving forward on kernel selection and compilation improvements, the compilers are reducing token cost by about 12% in our internal tests; i want to caveat that's pipeline-specific and contended workloads vary.
[00:55] Speaker 4 (Sofia): product, hi all. dedicated GA expanding next month, we now have two more regions for dedicated, and auto-scaling policies are more mature, also we're shipping a new routing policy UI. deck link in chat.
[01:15] Speaker 5 (Rahul): on the Dedicated benchmarks, we saw median p50 latency at our internal 2k token test ~110ms with batching enabled; spot cases spike under network contention, we'll share the spreadsheet with detailed histograms.
[01:36] Speaker 2 (Maya): thanks rahul, also want to call out a few customer wins this quarter — three mid-market customers went live on dedicated and told us saving was substantial vs in-house infra.
[01:52] Speaker 6 (Security lead, Aisha): security update — SOC2 readiness on track, audit scope refined, we plan control remediation by end of quarter. SSO/SAML improvements and KMS/HSM integration work is in progress. note: some acronyms in the doc got munged so please see the security repo link.
[02:12] Speaker 7 (Engineering PM): small note on private deployments — we shipped an updated VPC onboarding flow, customers can now bring their own KMS keys and we added extra logging for audit trails.
[02:33] Speaker 1 (Maya): hiring — we are pausing some non-critical hiring, we will still hire in priority areas (infra, security, sales for pipeline). this is a trimming, not a full freeze. managers will get guidance after this call.
[02:55] Speaker 8 (Sofia, faint): pricing question from slack — do we plan to lower hosted rates? answer: we are optimizing both sides, we won't race to bottom, rather focus on predictable economics per workload.
[03:15] Speaker 9 (Eng, question): can Dedicated handle GDPR data residency per region?
[03:22] Speaker 3 (Eli): yes — Dedicated can be pinned to region and we have controls for data retention, but for full legal residency we recommend Private with customer-managed VPC. there was a little cross talk.
[03:40] Speaker 10 (Customer success): any update on observability retention pricing?
[03:46] Speaker 4 (Sofia): yes, retention tiers are being refactored, new pricing options will be posted next week, and we'll let customer success pilot the designs.
[04:05] Speaker 11 (Maya): quick note about open-source and community — we released a reference app last month, engagement is high, but we need to keep the docs up to date.
[04:22] Speaker 12 (All-hands attendee): (murmur) can we get a deeper dive on the abort incident from last week?
[04:30] Speaker 3 (Eli): yeah, the spot instance scheduler had a race that caused a fallback to slower instances for a subset of traffic, we've pushed a hotfix and long-term mitigation is in review, postmortem to come.
[04:46] Speaker 13 (Security lead): question in hallway — SOC2 scope includes private deployment nodes? answer: audit will include control environment across hosted and dedicated, private will have contractual controls. again see security doc.
[05:05] Speaker 14 (Maya): ok moving to customer stories — marketing, could you summarize the Redwood-CloudX case?
[05:12] Speaker 15 (Marketing): CloudX moved to Dedicated for baseline traffic, they saw 40% lower per-token cost compared to their Naive self-hosting, we have a slide in the deck with cost model and assumptions. small transcription glitch: 'naive' sometimes reads as 'navy' in the notes.
[05:36] Speaker 16 (Product): Optimize toolkit updates — we added suggestions for batching thresholds and quantization profiles; initial results show 10-25% cost improvements on long-tail workloads.
[05:55] Speaker 17 (Maya): leadership asks — each org to submit two measurable OKRs tied to unit economics by next Friday.
[06:10] Speaker 18 (Q&A): will we open new sales assisted enterprise motion for EMEA region?
[06:18] Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, we are piloting with a partner in EMEA, more detail from GTM offline.
[06:30] Speaker 19 (Employee): what's the timeline for the SOC2 audit?
[06:36] Speaker 6 (Security lead): audit kickoff in September, final report expected by mid-November pending no major findings.
[06:50] Speaker 20 (Employee): how will this affect support SLAs?
[06:56] Speaker 2 (Maya): no immediate change to support SLAs, but enterprise customers on Dedicated will get SLA tiers with escalation paths.
[07:12] Speaker 3 (Eli): quick note — we've improved KV cache eviction to reduce tail latency; still tuning.
[07:25] Speaker 21 (Employee): request for more internal docs on model selection for workloads.
[07:31] Speaker 4 (Sofia): yes, we'll publish a model selection guide and a decision tree, should help sales and solutions.
[07:48] Speaker 22 (Employee): question about Private on-prem package maintenance windows?
[07:54] Speaker 17 (Product): we'll work with the customer per contract; standard is monthly windows, we can negotiate.
[08:10] Speaker 1 (Maya): ok, final recap — transparency, focusing on unit economics, targeted hiring, support Dedicated & Private growth.
[08:24] Speaker 1 (Maya): action items and follow-ups posted in the meeting notes, security will share SOC2 scope, rahul will share benchmarks.
[08:36] Speaker 1 (Maya): thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.
